meta.title: Who really said "All our dreams can come true, if we have the courage to pursue them"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: No evidence Walt Disney said it. The line first appears in print in 1992 — 26 years after his death — and Disney historians can’t verify it anywhere.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'All our dreams can come true, if we have the courage to pursue them'?
meta.ogDescription: Popularly pinned on Walt Disney, but unverified in his own words. Earliest print is a 1992 booklet; Disney historians call it apocryphal.

answer.label: Not Walt Disney — unverified & likely apocryphal
answer.authorName: No verified author (falsely credited to Walt Disney)
answer.authorDates: Earliest known print: 1992 — 26 years after Disney’s death
answer.sourceLine: This is a classic feel-good line pinned on Walt Disney with no primary source behind it. Disney Archives staff and historians (Marty Sklar, Jim Korkis, Jeff Kurti among them) report they “can’t find verification of that ANYWHERE,” and the earliest documented appearance is in The Goal Book (1992), p. vi — most likely derived from the Disneyland tagline “Where Dreams Come True” and “probably apocryphal.” Disney died in 1966; there is no record of him saying or writing this.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: Apocryphal — unverified in Disney’s own words
The Goal Book (R & E Publishers, 1992), p. vi

source.excerpt: All our dreams can come true, if we have the courage to pursue them.
trail: Disney historian Barry Linetsky files this under fake quotes, quoting a Disney Family Museum researcher: “We can’t find verification of that ANYWHERE … it doesn’t appear in publication” — after the Archives, WDI, Marty Sklar, Jim Korkis and Jeff Kurti all searched.
LibQuotes traces the earliest print to The Goal Book (1992), p. vi, and judges it “most likely derived from the tag line ‘Disneyland: Where Dreams Can Come True’ … probably apocryphal.”

On Wikiquote the only citation offered is Pat Williams’ 2004 biography How to Be Like Walt (p. 63) — a secondary compilation published decades after Disney’s death, not anything Disney himself said or wrote.
source.excerptNote: Also circulates as a second-person variant — “All your dreams can come true if you have the courage to pursue them” — which Wikiquote flags as an unsourced variant, a hallmark of a line with no fixed original text.

source.rightsNote: The exact wording has no identifiable author: its earliest located appearance is an anonymous 1992 goal-setting booklet, and no primary Disney source exists. Because the origin is unknown, no copyright or public-domain status can honestly be asserted.

author.name: Walt Disney
author.kicker: About the man it’s pinned on
author.heading: Walt Disney
author.metaLine: 1901–1966 · American animator, film producer & co-founder of The Walt Disney Company
author.bio: Walt Disney (1901–1966) was the American animator and entrepreneur behind Mickey Mouse, Snow White and Disneyland. Because his brand is built on dreams and imagination, uplifting “dream” lines are constantly manufactured and pinned to him — this quotation and the equally misattributed “If you can dream it, you can do it” being the two most common. His genuinely documented remarks tend to stress hard work and courage as action rather than aphorism.

cite.sourceCitation: Earliest documented in The Goal Book (Newport Beach, CA: R & E Publishers, 1992), p. vi, attributed to Walt Disney; no primary source in Disney’s own words has been located. See also Pat Williams, How to Be Like Walt (Deerfield Beach, FL: HCI, 2004), 63.

misattribution.heading: A feel-good line pinned on Disney
misattribution.intro: The quotation is everywhere on mugs, posters and graduation cards under Walt Disney’s name — but it cannot be traced to anything he actually said or wrote.

items.why: Disney Archives staff and historians report they cannot verify it in any Disney speech, film, letter or interview; a Disney Family Museum researcher told Barry Linetsky, “We can’t find verification of that ANYWHERE.” Its earliest known print appearance is 1992, 26 years after his death.

items.who: Pat Williams, How to Be Like Walt (2004)
items.why: Quote sites that do cite something point to Williams’ 2004 biography (Wikiquote, p. 63) — a modern compilation that repeats the attribution rather than a primary record of Disney’s words.

misattribution.truthLine: Best evidence: an apocryphal line first seen in print in 1992, likely spun off the Disneyland “Where Dreams Come True” tagline — not a documented Walt Disney quotation.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Disney
lead: Walt Disney’s entire brand is dreams-made-real, so a tidy sentence about dreams and courage feels unmistakably ‘his’ — which is exactly why it attaches to him so easily and resists correction. The line reads like distilled Disney marketing, and LibQuotes suggests it may in fact be a paraphrase of the Disneyland tagline “Where Dreams Come True” rather than a personal remark.

The same dynamic produced “If you can dream it, you can do it,” another perennial ‘Disney’ quote actually written by Imagineer Tom Fitzgerald years after Walt’s death. In both cases the sentiment is on-brand; the sourcing is not.
context.pull: It’s very ‘Wisdom-ish’ — but it doesn’t appear in publication.
